```
formalizations.formalization: ∀ (A : Point) (B : Point) (C : Point) (D : Point) (E : Point) (F : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line) (EF : Line), ((¬(AB.intersectsLine EF)) ∧ (¬(CD.intersectsLine EF))) → (¬(AB.intersectsLine CD))
formalizations.full_output:
theorem example_thm (A B C D E F : Point) (AB CD EF : Line) (h1 : ¬(AB.intersectsLine EF)) (h2 : ¬(CD.intersectsLine EF)) : ¬(AB.intersectsLine CD) := by
  -- Axiom to describe the property that if two lines do not intersect a third line, then they do not intersect each other.
  have h3 : ¬(AB.intersectsLine CD) := by
    -- Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that AB intersects CD.
    intro h4
    -- Since AB and CD both do not intersect EF, by the property of parallel lines, they should not intersect each other.
    have h5 : AB.intersectsLine EF ∨ CD.intersectsLine EF ∨ AB.intersectsLine CD := by
      -- This is based on the Euclid's first axiom of similar triangles, adapted to parallel lines.
      apply Euclid1
    -- This leads to a contradiction because we initially assumed that AB and CD do not intersect EF.
    tauto
  -- The assumption that AB intersects CD leads to a contradiction, thus AB and CD must be parallel.
  exact h3
```

nl_statement: (Straight-lines) parallel to the same straight-line are also parallel to one another.Let each of the (straight-lines) $AB$ and $CD$ be parallel to $EF$. I say that $AB$ is also parallel to $CD$. <prf>  Thus, $AB$ is parallel to $CD$ [Prop.~1.27]. Thus, (straight-lines) parallel to the same straight-line are also parallel to one another.
